title: Campbell
name: Campbell
metaTitle: Campbell 1031 Exchange Investors | San Jose, CA
metaDescription: 1031 exchange guidance for Campbell investors weighing Pruneyard-area retail, downtown Campbell Avenue storefronts, and creek-corridor multifamily.

sections.html: Campbell doesn't have the tech-campus skyline of its neighbors, and that's precisely the point for some exchangers — the city's commercial stock is smaller, older, and more walkable than what trades a few miles north. That smaller scale isn't a drawback for every exchanger — it simply means the underwriting has to rest on the individual building and tenant, not on a citywide tech-employer story.

sections.heading: The Pruneyard Sets the Ceiling for What Retail Here Commands
sections.html:
The Pruneyard Shopping Center has anchored Campbell's retail identity for decades, mixing shops, restaurants, and office space in a format that predates the newer mixed-use developments in surrounding cities. It remains the reference point most brokers use when pricing retail elsewhere in Campbell.

That reference point can mislead an exchanger evaluating a smaller freestanding retail building elsewhere in the city, since the Pruneyard's scale and tenant mix don't translate directly to a single-tenant pad a mile away. Price the specific building's own lease, not the shopping center's reputation.

sections.heading: A Narrower Shelf Than Its Neighbors
sections.html:
Campbell's commercial stock is narrower than its neighbors', concentrated in a few categories:

  • mixed retail and small office space around downtown Campbell Avenue
  • the Pruneyard's own retail and office component
  • smaller freestanding retail pads along Winchester Boulevard and Hamilton Avenue
  • garden-style multifamily converted or redeveloped along the Los Gatos Creek corridor
  • a limited stock of light-industrial and service-commercial buildings near the city's edges

sections.heading: Downtown's Walkability Is the Whole Value Proposition
sections.html:
Downtown Campbell Avenue has built its identity on restaurants, small shops, and a pedestrian-friendly layout that draws from Campbell itself and the surrounding cities, rather than competing on the office-employer density that drives leasing in San Jose or Santa Clara.

An exchanger evaluating downtown retail should underwrite it as a hospitality and small-shop market, checking actual foot traffic and tenant sales rather than assuming proximity to larger tech employers nearby carries the same weight it would in a corridor whose leasing is driven by office-employee density.

sections.heading: Residential Infill Is Competing With Commercial for the Same Parcels
sections.html:
Winchester Boulevard and several downtown-adjacent parcels have seen commercial buildings replaced or converted toward higher-density residential use in recent years, a pattern that reflects Campbell's limited land supply as much as any single project's merits.

An exchanger holding an older commercial parcel in one of these areas should factor in that residential conversion pressure when thinking about long-term hold value, since the highest-and-best use may no longer be commercial at all. A broker's asking price based on the parcel's commercial history alone may not reflect what a residential developer would actually pay for the same site today.

sections.heading: Small Purchase Price, Same Deadline
sections.html:
A Campbell property doesn't carry the same single-tenant concentration risk as a large NNN campus elsewhere in the metro, but it still needs the qualified intermediary, the tax advisor, and a lender reviewing the same file before the identification notice goes out.

Smaller deal size doesn't mean less risk of missing the deadline — a lender's appraisal on a converted or mixed-use building can take longer than expected, and the 180-day window closes with the gain still due regardless of purchase price. Confirm figures and deadlines with your own advisors; this page describes the market, not tax advice.

faqs.q: Does the Pruneyard's reputation set the price for other Campbell retail?
faqs.a: It shouldn't. Underwrite each building's own lease and tenant, since the Pruneyard's scale doesn't translate directly to a smaller freestanding pad.

faqs.q: How should I underwrite downtown Campbell Avenue retail?
faqs.a: As a hospitality and small-shop market driven by foot traffic, not as an extension of the office-employer demand that drives leasing in neighboring cities.

faqs.q: Is residential conversion pressure a real risk to commercial value here?
faqs.a: Yes, on some parcels. Limited land supply has pushed several commercial sites toward higher-density residential use, which can change the long-term highest-and-best-use calculation.

faqs.q: Do the standard identification rules apply to a smaller Campbell deal?
faqs.a: Yes, regardless of price. Up to three properties under the standard rule, or more under the 200% rule if combined value stays within twice what you sold.

faqs.q: What if my Campbell identification falls through near Day 45?
faqs.a: Have a genuinely underwritten backup ready and avoid taking receipt of exchange funds while you resolve it.

faqs.q: Is Campbell's retail demand tied to the same tech-employer growth that drives Santa Clara or Sunnyvale?
faqs.a: Only loosely. Downtown Campbell's retail leans on local residents and visitors drawn to its walkable character, not on office-employee lunch traffic the way corridors nearer the larger campuses do.

faqs.q: Does the Los Gatos Creek corridor support the same multifamily premium across all of Campbell?
faqs.a: No. The premium concentrates on properties genuinely close to the trail; a complex a half-mile away competes more directly with standard Campbell apartment stock.

faqs.q: Should a smaller Campbell commercial parcel be evaluated for its residential conversion potential?
faqs.a: It's worth checking, especially near Winchester Boulevard, where limited land supply has already pushed several comparable sites toward higher-density residential redevelopment.

faqs.q: How should I compare a Pruneyard-area lease to a smaller standalone Campbell retail lease?
faqs.a: Treat them as separate underwriting exercises. The Pruneyard's mixed-use scale and shared common areas create a different tenant experience and cost structure than a single-tenant pad, so pull comps within each category rather than blending the two.

faqs.q: Does Campbell's proximity to Los Gatos and San Jose meaningfully affect its own pricing?
faqs.a: Somewhat — brokers sometimes anchor Campbell pricing to whichever neighbor is trending hotter, so confirm the comp actually sits inside Campbell rather than being pulled from an adjacent city's very different market.
